card.name: Start of drug and metabolite names
card.fires_on: The first piece of a drug, metabolite or pharmacokinetic term that is split into parts, such as pro, N, A or n. It appears in interaction and pharmacokinetics text.

modes.label: Metabolite N- prefix
modes.description: The letter N starting a chemical name of an active metabolite, as in N-desmethyl.
modes.example: zolmitriptan and its active<< N>>-desmethyl metabolite were approximately doubled

modes.label: Start of a drug name
modes.description: The opening piece of a drug or drug class name that is split up, such as pro in propranolol or prodrug.
modes.example: the pharmacokinetics of metformin and<< pro>>pranolol, and metformin

modes.label: PK term start
modes.description: The first letter of a pharmacokinetic abbreviation like AUC.

card.writes: It pushes toward chemical-themed words, suggesting a chemical name or term comes next.
card.plain: It fires on the opening piece of a drug or metabolite name that is still being spelled out.
